english: Let $E$ be the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{12}=1$. Let $P$ be the point of $E$ with eccentric angle $\theta\in\left(\pi,\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ such that the tangent to $E$ at $P$ is parallel to the chord of $E$ whose midpoint is $\left(1,\dfrac32\right)$. The normal to $E$ at $P$ meets the $x$-axis at $(\alpha,0)$. Then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $E$ दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{12}=1$ है। माना $P$, $E$ का वह बिन्दु है जिसका उत्केन्द्र कोण $\theta\in\left(\pi,\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$ है तथा $P$ पर $E$ की स्पर्श रेखा, $E$ की उस जीवा के समान्तर है जिसका मध्यबिन्दु $\left(1,\dfrac32\right)$ है। $P$ पर $E$ का अभिलम्ब $x$-अक्ष को $(\alpha,0)$ पर मिलता है। तब $\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Chord with midpoint $(1,\tfrac32)$ ($T=S_1$): $\dfrac{x}{16}+\dfrac{y}{8}=\dfrac{1}{16}+\dfrac{3}{16}$, slope $-\dfrac12$ (the point is inside, as $\dfrac14<1$)
solution_full: The chord of $E$ with midpoint $(h,k)$ is $T=S_1$: $\dfrac{hx}{16}+\dfrac{ky}{12}=\dfrac{h^{2}}{16}+\dfrac{k^{2}}{12}$. For $\left(1,\dfrac32\right)$, which is inside $E$ since $\dfrac1{16}+\dfrac{9/4}{12}=\dfrac14<1$: $\dfrac{x}{16}+\dfrac{y}{8}=\dfrac14$, i.e. $x+2y=4$, slope $-\dfrac12$.
For $P(4\cos\theta,2\sqrt3\sin\theta)$ the tangent is $\dfrac{x\cos\theta}{4}+\dfrac{y\sin\theta}{2\sqrt3}=1$, with slope $-\dfrac{2\sqrt3\cos\theta}{4\sin\theta}=-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cot\theta$.

Parallel: $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cot\theta=\dfrac12$, so $\cot\theta=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$, giving $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ or $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$. Only $\theta=\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ lies in $\left(\pi,\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)$, so $P=\left(4\cdot\left(-\dfrac12\right),2\sqrt3\cdot\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)\right)=(-2,-3)$.
(Indeed $P$ lies on the line through the centre and the midpoint, $y=\dfrac32x$, as it must: the chords bisected on a diameter are parallel to the tangent at its end.)
originality_note: New: the point of contact is defined by parallelism with a chord known only through its midpoint, and the branch is fixed by the eccentric-angle interval before the normal is used (way 5). Closest known: equation of the chord bisected at a given point; normal at a given point. Different because: three standard steps are chained through a slope condition, and the student must choose the correct one of two eccentric angles.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that (1, 3/2) is inside E, that exactly one eccentric angle lies in (pi, 3pi/2), and that the answer is exact. Changed: No change.
key_step: Equate the slope of the T = S1 chord (-1/2) with the parametric tangent slope -(sqrt3/2) cot theta and choose theta = 4 pi/3.
justification: Three concepts chained (midpoint chord, parametric tangent, normal) with a branch choice; each step standard, numerical answer. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q2 (L3) on tangents of an ellipse; could be read as L2.
blueprint_concepts: Chord whose mid point is given for Ellipse

concept_use.Parametric coordinates for Ellipse: P is described by its eccentric angle theta in (pi, 3pi/2); the parametric slope -(sqrt3/2) cot theta gives theta = 4 pi/3 and P(-2,-3).
concept_use.Tangent and normal for Ellipse: The tangent at P supplies the slope condition, and the normal at P, 16x/x1 - 12y/y1 = 4, gives the intercept alpha = -1/2.
concept_use.Chord whose mid point is given for Ellip: The chord with midpoint (1, 3/2) is found by T = S1 as x + 2y = 4, slope -1/2, which fixes the direction of the tangent.
